summary: Obfuscated remote-controlled shell/PTY agent with runtime self-replacement
details: The npm package @whalent/agent-core ships a 13.6 MB main/bin entry `dist/index.cjs` that is heavily obfuscated with javascript-obfuscator (string-array + numeric-wrapper scheme, decoder `a0_0x1cb7`, rotating string array of length 105679), hiding all URLs, hostnames, and command names behind a runtime string-reconstruction layer. The bundle links a network transport (WebSocket via undici, plus `ssh2` as a runtime dependency and `node-pty` as an optional dependency) to local shell/PTY execution: decoded strings reference `process.env.SHELL`, `127.0.0.1:3389` (RDP), `127.0.0.1:5900`/`5901` (VNC), cross-spawn, and repeated `daemon`/`upgrade` tokens — the shape of a network-to-shell dispatcher that hands remote-supplied bytes to a local shell on the installer's host. The README additionally states that this package `is the package replaced by remote daemon upgrades`, meaning the running agent overwrites its own installed code with content fetched from a remote server at runtime; the bundle contains `new Function(` / `Function(` sinks and the destination URL is not verifiable because it is obfuscated. Together these mechanisms give the package operator interactive shell/PTY access to the installer host and an unbounded remote-code-load channel with no version pinning or integrity check exposed to the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
